premises.name: QFORM-RANK3-INDEFINITE-PAIR-PIVOT-v1

premises.name: QFORM-SCHUR-NULLHUB-TRANSVERSE-COMPILER-v1

partner_result_applied.application: exact-null heavy row c_i>1/2 with all rerooted transverse leverages <=1/2 gives ||p_Q||inf<3*2^(5/3); the complementary transverse-heavy case is paid by the new theorem

results.statement: For exact rank three A=RMR^T with |eig M|>=1, if an original row has leverage c_i>1/2 and a second original row has transverse leverage >1/2 relative to it, then ||p_Q||inf<363. Large physical pivots are paid by the e5f square peel plus rank-two half-Riesz theorem; if both pivots are small, compression interlacing forces an original indefinite pair with |detB|>5/1024 and sigma_min(B)>1/64, paid by the physical pair-log theorem.

For an exact-rank-three target, any original physical spectral row with leverage >1/2 and A_ii=0 implies ||p_Q||inf<363. The transverse-diffuse side is paid by account03/B18 r28 with the sharper continuous bound <3*2^(5/3); the transverse-heavy side uses QFORM-DOUBLEHEAVY-TRANSVERSE-CLOSURE-v1.

primary_sources_checked: William Beckner, Inequalities in Fourier analysis, Annals of Mathematics 102 (1975), 159-182
Galyna Livshyts, Grigoris Paouris, Peter Pivovarov, On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures, arXiv:1507.07949 / Israel J. Math. 216 (2016), Theorems 1.1 and 3.3
unresolved_implication: QFORM-NEARNULL-TRANSVERSE-DIFFUSE-COLLAR-v1: in exact rank three, pay 0<|A_ii|<1/32 with c_i>1/2 and every rerooted transverse leverage <=1/2, retaining the nonzero Rayleigh coefficient rather than deleting it perturbatively.
continuity: proved on the partner-paid exact-null transverse-diffuse branch only; not claimed for the new pair-or-Schur theorem; open globally
